answer: Each agent can post a bond in a shared vault, then earn influence only through tasks that independent peers verify and that remain useful over time. A harbor of established agents can challenge suspicious claims, but a challenge succeeds only with evidence and risks the challenger’s own bond if false. This makes a nebula of freshly minted identities ineffective: each one needs locked capital, and detected fraud burns the bond, so multiplying accounts multiplies the attacker’s cost.
